references.text: Jacob went down to Egypt with his family, who were few in number, just as described in the confession.
Abraham went down to Egypt because of a famine, a pattern that repeats itself in Israel's history.
Isaac was the son of an Aramean father from Paddan-Aram, which refers to 'my father was a wandering Aramean'.
Laban is called the Aramean, and Jacob lived with him, which explains the expression 'wandering Aramean'.
Laban is called the Aramean, and Jacob fled from him as a wandering foreigner.
The Israelites came to Egypt with few people, but became a great and mighty nation there.
Pharaoh acknowledges that the Israelites have become a great and mighty people, fulfilling the confession.
Stephen's speech describes how Jacob went down to Egypt with 75 people and the people grew and became numerous.
A reminder of Abraham as the ancestor, when he was one and became many, parallel to the theme of growth from few to many.
The origin of Jerusalem is described with an Aramaic and Canaanite background, reflecting the confession about the ancestors' origins.
